The sound of an emergency siren typically varies by location, but it is often a loud, wailing tone that alternates between high and low pitches. The specific pattern and duration can differ between regions and jurisdictions.

The annual siren test is usually conducted on a specific date each year, often in the spring or fall. In the United States, for example, many communities perform siren tests on the first Sunday in September. However, the exact date and time can vary depending on the local government or emergency management agency. It's best to check with your local authorities for the precise date and time of the test in your area.
